segments: The eleventh dynasty:
The Hunnic (Mongol) kings.
On Wednesday, the twenty-eighth
of the Latter Tishri of that same year,
when the Ninevites (people of Mosul) heard of the calamity that had happened there,
they were terrified and very greatly afraid. And as the nobles and commanders crossed over to the region of Mosul,
certain men, lovers of toil and bearers of the hardships of the holy churches, approached them,
and took upon themselves [to pay] a large amount of gold.
And because they did not possess anything from the goods of this world,
they laid hands upon the vessels of the churches,
and they did not leave a cross, or an icon, or a censer, or a Gospel book bound with gold or silver, that they did not take.
And when this was not sufficient,
they also assessed a certain levy on the believers in the cities and in the villages,
and gathered nearly fifteen thousand dinars,
and weighed them out to avert the destruction of the churches and the tribute of the Christians.
And by the help of God, not a single church was harmed.
And in those days, a certain tribe of the Mongols,
who were called the Oirats,
who inhabited the surroundings of the Monastery of Mar Matthew,
happened to incur the anger of the King of Kings.
And envoys kept coming from him to them,
threatening and menacing [them].
And because in the days when Baidu reigned,
these Oirats had laid hands on certain Turcomans,
and had taken from them sheep, herds of cattle, droves of horses, mares, mules, and camels without number,
after the kingdom of Baidu came to an end,
and Ghazan took power,
a command went out that they should return and take all the property of the Turcomans back from the Oirats;
and whoever resisted and would not be persuaded,
should die the death.
And because the greater part of these possessions had been consumed,
and nothing of them was left at all in the hands of the Oirats,
for this reason they suffered great distress, and were harassed by the envoys, and very much so by the Turcomans,
and {great damage was brought? OCR} into the midst of the believers.
And to this wrath another wrath was added {OCR?}:
another [trouble].
Now there was among the Tatars {OCR?} a certain tribe of Mongols,
who were called Oirats,
who inhabited the surroundings of the monastery of Mar Matthew.
They incurred a certain indignation from him {OCR?}.
